transcript: Your slide deck already explains something well. Here's how to make it work without you in the room, by turning it into a video.
A deck on its own relies on a presenter. A video carries the slides and the explanation, so anyone can watch whenever suits them, and everyone hears the same message.
You have three ways to convert: export from PowerPoint, record your screen, or use a dedicated converter that builds the video from your notes.
Tidy the deck first. Keep one idea per slide, make each headline the point, and move detail into the speaker notes, where it becomes narration.
Your speaker notes are your script. Write spoken sentences, not reminders. They run longer, but they're much easier to follow by ear.
Upload your deck, pick a voice, and download the MP4. Try Basic first. On Pro, AI directs an animated explainer. Visit powerpoint2vid.com.
